creator.name: Fellaswimming
creator.expertise: Software engineer with 3+ years of experience, heavy in frontend and mobile (Next.js, React.js, Flutter). Beginner in backend with familiarity in Supabase, Firebase, and Convex.
creator.background: I am a software engineer with 3+ years of frontend/mobile experience, and also the owner of Fellaswimming, a swim school in Sidoarjo, Indonesia that has been running for 5 years. The business started small and was manageable via WhatsApp and Excel, but as it grew, leads coming in from Instagram and TikTok became overwhelming and manual operations became a bottleneck: data getting stuck, follow-ups slipping through the cracks, prospective customers having to repeatedly ask about schedules. As the engineer in the room, I finally said 'enough' and started building a proper system, leveraging my own engineering skills to professionalize Fellaswimming's operations. Not outsourcing, not buying a generic template, but building it myself so I can iterate quickly as the business evolves.

purpose.whoYouHelp: Parents in Sidoarjo and surrounding areas with children ages 3 to 12, plus teens and adults learning to swim, plus families wanting to take lessons together. Spanning budget tiers from affordable group classes to premium private and semi-private with certified coaches and small classes. What unites them: they care about safety, structured curriculum, and coach quality, not just 'so my child does not drown'.
purpose.problemYouSolve: Two interconnected primary problems sit at the center. First, the discovery and trust gap: prospective customers struggle to find and validate credible swim schools in Sidoarjo because most schools have only scattered info on Instagram and TikTok, with no single place to see curriculum, coach credentials, prices, schedules, and locations. Second, the education gap: parents often do not know what matters when choosing a swim school (curriculum structure, coach to student ratio, certified coaches), so they default to price alone, turning the market into a race to the bottom. A secondary problem is registration friction: the entire booking pipeline lives in WhatsApp DMs that do not scale, with leads getting lost in spreadsheets.
purpose.desiredTransformation: On the user side, parents make confident decisions within a week (down from weeks of indecision or defaulting to the closest option). After scrolling the landing page and reading 2 to 3 articles, they understand what matters (curriculum structure, certified coaches, class size), can clearly compare Fellaswimming's options, and register without WhatsApp back and forth. Their child starts lessons with realistic expectations from day one. On the market side, Sidoarjo gets one go-to reference for serious swim education. Fellaswimming becomes the obvious choice for parents who research thoroughly, not through aggressive marketing but because its online presence and educational content prove its quality. Leads come in with high intent (they have already read articles and seen coach profiles), and lead-to-trial conversion rises significantly.
purpose.whyYou: Three reinforcing layers of founder-market fit. First, a rare hybrid skill set: very few swim school owners in Sidoarjo are also software engineers. I know the operational pain from the inside (5 years running the business, dealing directly with manual WhatsApp and Excel) and I have the skills to build it myself without outsourcing or buying a generic template, so every feature truly fits Fellaswimming's workflow and can be iterated quickly. Second, first-hand pain credibility: I live inside this problem daily. 5 years of handling leads from social media, feeling the exhaustion of WhatsApp follow-ups, watching customer data sprawl across spreadsheets. I know exactly which questions parents ask repeatedly (schedules, prices per class type, locations). This website is not an assumption, it is a solution born from real experience. Third, long-term commitment plus local grounding: 5 years building Fellaswimming proves I am in this for the long haul, not as a side project. I have local networks in Sidoarjo (existing parents, coaches, pool relationships) that no digital-only competitor can replicate. Plus the engineering skill means the tech can scale with the business without being tied to an agency or freelancer.

product.name: Fellaswimming
product.oneLiner: Fellaswimming is the most informative swim school in Sidoarjo, where families learn first, then register with confidence.
product.howItWorks: A parent Googles 'best swim lessons for kids in Sidoarjo' or gets a link from a friend. The landing page opens with an honest tagline. Interested but not yet ready to register, they open the Articles tab and read 2 to 3 pieces ('Right age to start swim lessons', 'Private vs semi vs group: what is the difference', 'Signs of a competent swim coach'). After feeling more confident, they return to the landing page, pick the class type that fits, and register. They become customers with proper expectations from day one.
keyCapabilities: Comprehensive responsive landing page (hero showcase, class types, coach highlights, gallery, testimonials, Google Maps embedded location, primary CTA to register) optimized for mobile-first and SEO-friendly content.
Dedicated registration page with a 3-step wizard form (low friction, mobile-friendly, validation per step) culminating in a confirmation summary.
Public articles section (index + detail) with SEO-optimized URLs and metadata, designed for educational content marketing aligned with the 'learn first, then register' positioning.

Admin dashboard (desktop only) with email + password authentication, an overview home (counters + recent leads + quick links), registration management (list view + modal actions for status update, WhatsApp deep link, internal notes; no detail page), and an article CMS with a Tiptap rich-text editor that uploads images to Supabase Storage.
Minimal testimonials CMS (desktop-only admin) covering list, add/edit/delete, and a featured toggle to control which testimonials appear on the landing page.
product.marketDifferentiation: Unlike other swim schools in Sidoarjo that are passive on Instagram with scattered information, Fellaswimming offers comprehensive educational content (articles + an informative landing page) that helps parents do proper research before registering. Choosing swim lessons for a child is too important to be judged from three Instagram slides.
product.magicMoment: A parent scrolls Fellaswimming and reads an article like 'Right age to start swim lessons' or 'Private vs semi vs group: what is the difference'. Something clicks: they realize there is a clear framework to evaluate swim schools, not just 'find one nearby and cheap'. At the end of the article, a subtle CTA reads: 'Pick the Fellaswimming class that fits your child'. They click, and the landing page literally answers the questions they just learned to ask. The 'oh, this is a swim school that gets it' moment.

audience.primaryUser: Mama Risa, 38, full-time mom in upper-middle-class Sidoarjo with 2 children (ages 5 and 8). Native Indonesian speaker, follows parenting accounts on Instagram (such as @keluargakita), researches thoroughly before any decision for her kids. Frustrated because no swim school in Sidoarjo offers parenting-style content: descriptions are either generic or worse, too aggressively hard-sell.
secondaryUsers: Husband/dad (decision-maker): co-signer on the decision. Risa researches, the husband signs off and approves the budget. He browses the landing page for 5 to 10 minutes to validate before approving. Needs trust-building info (coach, curriculum, pricing) without deep parenting context.

Children ages 5 to 12 (beneficiary, actual end-user): the ones who attend the lessons. On mobile they enjoy looking at gallery photos of the pool and coaches. Visual content must be accessible for pre-readers and young readers.

Fellaswimming non-IT staff (operator): users of the admin dashboard. Not tech-savvy, so the UI must be highly intuitive. They deliver Fellaswimming's value to prospective customers, so admin UX directly impacts conversion.
audience.currentAlternatives: Direct competitors are other swim schools in Sidoarjo active on Instagram and TikTok (solo coaches or small 1 to 2 branch schools); the ones that stand out usually post training videos frequently. Adjacent tools misused for the same job: Google Maps search ('swim lessons Sidoarjo'), Instagram explore and hashtag search, Facebook parenting groups for Sidoarjo. Manual workarounds include asking in neighborhood or school WhatsApp groups, or hiring freelance swim coaches who hang around public pools.
audience.frustrations: Functional pain: Mama Risa has to open 5 to 7 tabs (Instagram accounts for swim schools A, B, C, Google Maps reviews, screenshots in WhatsApp groups). Each account only posts promotions without complete info. She has to DM each account one by one to ask about prices, schedules, exact locations, and slot availability. Responses come at unpredictable hours (sometimes 6 hours, sometimes 2 days). Comparing becomes impossible because each school's response format is different. She ends up picking 'the one that responded first and was most polite' rather than the best fit. Emotional pain: she reads hard-sell IG captions ('Your child must learn to swim!' with fire emojis) but no concrete information. She feels treated like an ad target, not like a parent seriously seeking a solution. If she asks in the comments, she gets template responses ('Please DM us 😊'). She feels undervalued as a customer doing thorough research, a stark contrast to pediatricians or hospitals that treat her as a decision-making partner.

business.initialGoal: Within 90 days: 150 to 200 registration leads via the website form (vs nearly 100% via WhatsApp previously); 8 to 12 articles published with 2,000+ total views (organic SEO starting to work); top 5 on Google for at least 2 'swim lessons Sidoarjo' keywords; 1 article shared organically in a Sidoarjo WhatsApp parenting community; 40%+ lead-to-trial conversion rate.
business.sixMonthVision: Within 6 months: 600 to 800 total registration leads (steady 100+/month); 25+ articles published with organic search becoming the #1 traffic source (overtaking Instagram and TikTok referrals); top 3 for 5+ Sidoarjo keywords and top 10 for regional Surabaya keywords; tactical expansion such as 1 to 2 new class types or schedules, or partnerships with local PAUD and TK kindergartens for institutional referrals; 1 to 2 video testimonials shot for the landing page (premium social proof); 50%+ of leads cite Fellaswimming's content as the source of their decision when asked.
business.constraints: Solo execution: I handle everything myself (development, decisions, initial content writing). Part-time and tight: about 10 to 15 hours per week (the rest goes to running the swim school). Backend skill gap: I am familiar with Supabase but still a beginner, so I must be cautious with RLS, migrations, and edge cases. Tight budget: prefer free tiers (Vercel free, Supabase free or Pro at $25/month max). Content: I write the initial 5 to 10 articles myself (about 3 to 5 hours per article). MVP timeline target: 8 to 10 weeks given these constraints.
business.goToMarket: Pure organic content + existing social media. Cross-post article snippets to existing Instagram and TikTok to drive traffic to the website. SEO long-tail focus for Sidoarjo with keyword research and per-article optimization for specific queries ('right age to start kids swim lessons', 'private vs semi vs group', 'when is a child ready for the deep end'). Articles designed for WhatsApp share (clean meta previews, quotable opening paragraphs). Convert the existing Instagram and TikTok audience into website visitors as a launch boost. Cost: Rp 0, only time. Paid ads and influencer partnerships are deferred to a post-MVP phase if needed.

feeling.brandPersonality: Friendly Guide. A peer parent who has walked the journey first. Relatable, encouraging, transparent, and candid. Like a parent friend who has already gone through this and shares insights honestly. Modern and casual, but still respectful about the urgency of child safety. A peer to parents, not a brand talking down to them.
feeling.visualMood: Soft Aquatic. Palette tends toward clear sky blues, soft turquoise, sandy beige, with a soft coral accent. Rounded sans-serif typography throughout (candidates: Plus Jakarta Sans, Nunito, Manrope) for a playful but readable feel. Energy is refreshing and lightly playful with subtle bubble or water motifs as micro illustrations (not photos). Reference touchpoints: 'Duolingo light' approachability, 'Headspace calm' breathing room, and Indonesian parenting brands like @keluargakita.
feeling.toneOfVoice: Friendly and clear, like chatting with another parent at a playground. Not too formal, not too casual. Always specific and straight to the point, avoiding jargon. Personalized address mix: 'Bunda/Ayah' (warm and inclusive) in headlines and greetings, 'kamu' (peer-friendly modern Indonesian) in body and instructions, and dropping the address for neutral functional fields. Example greeting: 'Hai Bunda/Ayah, lagi cari les renang yang tepat untuk si kecil?' Example CTA: 'Lihat Jadwal Kelas'. Example error: 'Form belum lengkap. Cek bagian Kontak ya.' Example success: 'Pendaftaran terkirim! Tim Fellaswimming akan WhatsApp kamu dalam 1x24 jam.'
feeling.antiPatterns: Never feel like corporate marketing: no generic stock photos of happy kids in pools, no hard-sell exclamations ('Buruan! Promo terbatas!'), no formal corporate jargon ('Kami sangat senang bisa melayani Anda'), no forcing users to DM for basic info that should be on the website. Never feel childish: no cartoon water mascots or comic-style illustrations, no neon or rainbow gradients, no jokey emojis in instructional copy, no patronizing tone ('Ayo Bunda jangan ragu lagi'). Never feel clinical or formal: no clinical white-coat photography, no heavy academic serif body text, no dense paragraphs without breaks (mobile readability dies), no top-down educator tone ('Dalam kajian kami...').

frontend.rationale: App Router with React Server Components delivers SEO-grade SSR/ISR, ideal for the content-heavy article strategy. Largest ecosystem with mature integrations (Tailwind, shadcn, Supabase SSR). Founder is already proficient (3+ years of Next.js and React). Mobile-first responsive is straightforward with Tailwind. Vercel one-click deploy on the free tier. Targeting Next.js 16; note that v16 introduces the proxy.ts convention (replacing middleware.ts) and Supabase SSR docs still reference middleware but the pattern adapts cleanly.

backend.rationale: Managed PostgreSQL + Auth + Storage + Edge Functions + Row-Level Security. Relational fit for content-heavy multi-entity data (registrations, articles, testimonials, categories). Founder is familiar with Supabase. Free tier covers MVP (500MB DB, 1GB storage, 50k MAU). Storage built-in for article cover images and Tiptap inline image uploads. RLS separates public-read (published articles) from admin-write. Known gotcha to plan for: anon INSERT...RETURNING fails without a SELECT policy, so registration submission uses a service-role server client.

database.rationale: Native pairing with Supabase backend. PostgreSQL v17, automatic backups, point-in-time recovery on paid tiers. Excellent fit for Fellaswimming's relational use case (registrations referencing class types, articles with categories and authors, testimonials with featured flags). Free tier provides 500MB storage which is more than enough for MVP.

auth.rationale: Native integration with Supabase backend. JWT-based with RLS integration. For Fellaswimming MVP, only email + password is required for admin users (simpler for non-IT staff), plus a forgot-password flow (email reset link). Public surfaces have no auth. Always use getUser() not getSession() for authorization decisions (getSession is unverified cookie data per Supabase SSR docs).

payments.rationale: No online payment in scope. Fellaswimming.com is a lead-gen + ops tool for an offline business; all payments happen offline (bank transfer or cash at the school) after the WhatsApp follow-up. Skipping payment integration keeps MVP scope tight and avoids unnecessary friction in the registration funnel. Payment integration can be reconsidered in a future phase if the business decides to collect deposits or fees online.
